records.name: Philadelphia Liberty Tennis Association
records.summary: A tennis group open to LGBTQ+ players and allies across the Philadelphia area and the wider Delaware Valley. It runs drills and events and is a USTA community tennis association.
records.what_you_do: Members play tennis with the group, practice in drills at Riverwinds Golf and Tennis Club in West Deptford, New Jersey, and take part in indoor winter and outdoor summer leagues and social events.

schedule.text: Drills at Riverwinds Golf and Tennis Club in West Deptford, New Jersey, are held on Saturday afternoons, starting around 2 pm, on dates posted on the events page.

locations.label: Drill venue: Riverwinds Golf and Tennis Club
locations.address: 70 Eagle Point Rd, West Deptford, NJ 08086

cost.text: Each drill costs $35 per person, paid at the club or in the booking app. A current yearly membership is required to join drills, and the membership price is not published.

first_step.how: Join through the JOIN US link on the website, then book a Riverwinds drill on the CourtReserve booking site that the drills page points to.
first_step.basis: The group invites non-members to its social events and runs one drill group for all levels, but drills need a current membership and a booking first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Drills bring together players of every level in one group, and each session costs $35. The page asks you to update your playing level on your member profile, and to email the board if you are unsure of your level.
first_visit_tips: Email board@philadelphialibertytennis.org if you are not sure which level to choose.
Keep your membership current, because lapsed memberships do not qualify for drills.
Pay in the app ahead of time or at the club on the day.
Cancel early, since a no-show or last-minute cancellation is charged.

records.notes: The event page header lists 10 Oct 2026 with a 2 pm start, but its body lists Saturdays in July and August with no year and gives two different end times (3:30 pm and 4 pm). This record uses only the header date and the 2 pm start. Yearly dues are not published. The site has no FAQ, accessibility, parking or new-member page. The drill venue is in New Jersey, so its location is marked as outside the city. Tier 1 cost text said fees were not stated; the drill fee of $35 is now recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Action
records.summary: A youth leadership group for middle and high school students in Philadelphia. It trains students in civic leadership, pairs them with mentors and funds student civic projects.
records.what_you_do: Students join one of three programs: Junior Youth Action for 7th and 8th graders, Inspiring Leaders for 9th and 10th graders (a two-year program), and Service Leaders for graduates of the first two. Adults can apply to be facilitators, who get training to coach and mentor students.

schedule.text: Junior Youth Action holds leadership sessions about twice a month, and Inspiring Leaders holds bimonthly training sessions with mentor check-ins at least every two weeks. Volunteer trips happen about once a quarter. Meeting days and times are not published.

cost.text: No student fee is named on the program pages. The Inspiring Leaders program funds a student service project of up to $5,000.

first_step.how: Call 215-867-9464 or email inspire@youthactionteam.org to ask whether applications for your grade are open this school year.
first_step.basis: Each program asks students to apply through an online form, and the pages do not describe the selection or confirm that applications are open for the current year.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pages do not describe a first session or an information night. Once in, students attend leadership sessions about twice a month, meet a mentor one on one, and help plan events, and Junior Youth Action students can log up to 20 hours of service. Volunteer trips to help local organizations happen about once a quarter.
first_visit_tips: Ask which program and application round are open, since the program pages still name the 2024 to 2025 service year.
Ask where sessions meet, because the pages list only a P.O. Box.
Ask about costs and scholarship help, which the pages mention without amounts.
Ask whether a parent or guardian needs to take part in the application.

records.notes: The program pages still name the 2024 to 2025 service year for applications, and no 2026 to 2027 application notice was found. A search summary said applications were open for 2024 to 2025, which is out of date, so it is not used. The January 2026 MLK Day of Service post is the newest dated item; its date came from the homepage link and a search result, and the post itself was not opened. Impact figures on the site show placeholder zeros, so they are not used. Service Leaders is for graduates of the two programs, who can earn at least 50 service hours a year and receive funding for up to six projects; graduates contact their program leader. Tier 1 contact details are unchanged.

records.name: Philly Cheer Elite
records.summary: An all-volunteer cheerleading team in Philadelphia that uses cheer to raise awareness of LGBTQIA+ equality.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer members join either as performing members, who cheer and stunt, or as production members, who handle behind the scenes logistics. The team raises funds and donates to organizations that support LGBTQ+ people.

schedule.text: Practices are on Monday evenings from 7:30 to 10:30 pm at a practice location in North Philadelphia. The site does not give a street address for it.

cost.text: The join page does not list dues or fees. The team takes donations through a PayPal fundraiser.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form linked from the join page to be added to the recruitment list for upcoming recruitment events.
first_step.basis: The only published way in is an interest form that adds you to a list, and the pages do not describe tryouts or what happens after the form, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The team describes its members as LGBTQIA+ and ally adults, and calls itself all-volunteer. Practices run Monday evenings from 7:30 to 10:30 pm, and the team says it will tell people about recruitment events. The pages do not describe tryouts, skill requirements, dues, or time commitment, so ask before you commit.
first_visit_tips: Fill out the interest form first, since it is the only route the site publishes.
Email info@phillycheerelite.org to ask whether a tryout or skills check comes before the first practice.
Ask for the exact practice address, because the site gives only a mailing address.
Plan for three hours on Monday evenings, since practice runs 7:30 to 10:30 pm.

records.notes: The join page gives Monday practice times at a North Philadelphia location, but the About page's Practice Location heading gives only the mailing address, so no practice street address is recorded. The footer reads 2019, which is not evidence of current activity, so status stays probably active. Tier 1 said there was no membership fee; the pages do not state fees at all, so the cost text is corrected. The mission page names Cheer Athletics Philadelphia (on the About page) and Safe Space Alliance (a logo badge), neither with a link. There is no events page; the team books appearances by email. The pro shop is run by a third party and is not recorded.

records.name: Philly Girls Baseball
records.summary: A nonprofit all-girls baseball program in Philadelphia for players ages 8 to 18, with teams, tournaments, and a need for volunteer coaches.
records.what_you_do: Girls join teams called the Philly Flames, practice in the spring and summer, and play tournaments through the fall. The group is adding volunteer coaches, who must complete a background check, abuse awareness training and Pitch Smart training.

schedule.text: The outdoor season runs March through October. Sunday afternoon practices run from late March through June, and weekday evening practices happen one or two times a week in summer, with off weeks during tournaments.

cost.text: The 2026 instructional package is $180 per player and the all-inclusive package is $600 per player, both payable in installments. Instructional players pay extra for tournaments, and scholarships are available on request.

first_step.how: Register for the instructional package through the group's LeagueApps registration page, which takes sign-ups on a rolling basis.
first_step.basis: The instructional package says all experience levels are welcome, registration is rolling, and the site gives a clear route for coaches and for scholarship requests.
first_step.what_to_expect: The instructional package covers practices, clinics and scrimmages, plus a jersey, a hat and a team weekend called Big Baseball Weekend with DC Girls Baseball. Tournaments cost extra for instructional players, so ask about the fees before you sign up. Practices fall on Sunday afternoons from late March through June, and on weekday evenings in summer.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own glove, cleats, helmet and equipment bag, since helmets are not shared.
Wear baseball or athletic pants that allow sliding, with no shorts or leggings, and a forward facing cap.
Families provide the pants, belts and socks; the group provides the jerseys and hats.
Ask in advance for a team bat if you do not have one.

records.notes: Prices are the 2026 figures from the homepage. The FAQ mixes 2024 and 2025 wording, so only its general equipment and uniform rules are used. The background check applies to volunteer coaches; the pages do not require one for players. The DMV Series in Maryland (Oct 10 to 11, 2026) is a dated event, so it is used only for the last sign of life and kept out of the schedule text. The LeagueApps registration page opened to a generic member portal with no details, so it is not a source. Chew Field and D. Finnegan are named as practice fields with no street addresses, so they are not recorded as locations. The two IRS addresses are the same street in two spellings and are kept as tier 1 had them. The website is updated to the https address the site uses.

records.name: Rebel Ventures
records.summary: A youth-run healthy food business where high school students develop healthy food products, sell them to schools, and work with kids on cooking and hands-on learning.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can help with branding and graphic design, video documentation, or in-person kitchen and office work, and the team says roles can be shaped around what a person can add. High school students can check the jobs page for openings, and adults can apply to mentor through a form on the mentor page.

first_step.how: Email rebelventures215@gmail.com with the help you can offer, such as design, video, or kitchen and office work.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page welcomes all volunteers and gives an email to start, but it sets no sign-up steps, start dates or training.
first_step.what_to_expect: The volunteer page describes design, video, and in-person kitchen and office work, with roles shaped around what you can add. It does not describe shifts, a time commitment, training, or background checks. Your first contact is an email about your skills, so expect that conversation before any placement.
first_visit_tips: Say in your first email what you can offer, such as design, video, or kitchen and office help.
High school students who need service hours can say so, since the page welcomes them.
Ask about time commitment and training, which the pages do not describe.
Check the jobs page again before applying for paid work, because it said the team was not hiring when we checked on 2026-10-08.

records.notes: Tier 1 described the volunteer role as kitchen or office only; the volunteer page also lists design and video work. The high school jobs page said the team is not hiring at the moment, with no date given. The mentor page says paid mentor roles are for college and graduate students; it does not say whether professional volunteers are paid. The IRS data had a second address line holding only the PO Box number (8381), so it was dropped as a duplicate fragment. The homepage names a Rebel Chefs Live event with no date. No kitchen or office street address is published.

records.name: Restore Salon Services
records.summary: Stylists give free haircuts and styling to people who cannot get to a salon because of illness, disability or displacement, including at hospitals, rehab centers and at home.
records.what_you_do: Licensed stylists visit clients at homes, hospitals, rehab centers and skilled nursing facilities. Clients ask for a visit through the request form on the services page. Stylists, volunteers and sponsors can sign up on the Join Our Village page.

schedule.text: Free visits at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania every Monday, at Jefferson Moss-Magee Rehabilitation on the third Sunday of each month, and in weekly three-hour sessions at Ronald McDonald House Charities in Philadelphia. Home visits are also offered, and the site does not give set times for them.

cost.text: Free for clients. Donations are taken through the Circle of Care page, by card or by Venmo.

first_step.how: If you need a visit, fill out the request form linked from restoresalonservices.org/services, and expect a team member to reach out after you submit it.
first_step.basis: Anyone who needs a visit can use a public request form and the page says staff will follow up, though the site does not describe volunteer training or what happens after a volunteer signs up.
first_step.what_to_expect: A licensed stylist comes to you at a home, hospital, rehab center or care facility, and can cut, style, blow-dry, do up-dos, buzz cuts, wig styling and barber work for all hair types, starting in infancy. Caregivers and family members are also served. The site does not say how long a visit lasts or how soon one can be booked, though testimonials on the site mention private rooms and gentle handling.
first_visit_tips: Expect a call or email from the team after you submit the request form, since the site does not say how soon.
Ask about parking or transit before a visit, because the site lists neither.
Use the services request form for a visit; the Circle of Care page is a donation form.
Helpers: the stylist form asks for the days you can work from Monday to Saturday and a short bio.

records.notes: Tier 1 told visitors to use the Circle of Care form to ask for a visit. That is wrong: the Circle of Care page is a donation form, and visit requests go through the services page. The Join Our Village page says all volunteers are licensed and have completed a background check, so the background check flag applies to volunteers, not to clients. The footer links an accessibility statement that could not be read, so no access details are recorded. Partner sites named on the homepage (the hospital, the rehab center, Ronald McDonald House Charities) have no links. The homepage also mentions a separate Board and Sponsors page, which was not opened.

records.name: RISE Philadelphia
records.summary: Online one-on-one tutoring for students from kindergarten through 12th grade in Philadelphia and South Jersey, matched with graduate student tutors. Also offers college application help for high school students.
records.what_you_do: Graduate students tutor students one on one, online, in subjects such as math, science, English, social studies and world languages. Families start with a participation form that parents and students both sign, and tutors apply through an interest form on the site. The team also offers college prep help, such as AP courses, SAT and ACT prep, Common App help, and financial aid.

first_step.how: Families: use the I need a tutor option on risephiladelphia.com to start the participation form, which parents and students both sign.
first_step.basis: Families and tutors each have a public sign-up route, and the site says the team will reach out up to three times to make a match, but the pages do not describe screening, session details or cost.
first_step.what_to_expect: After you sign the participation form, the team tries to match your student with a graduate tutor and contacts you up to three times to do it. Sessions are one on one and online, and the team picks tutors with each student's needs and academic background in mind. The pages do not say how long a session lasts, how often it happens, or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Have your student's grade and the subjects you need ready, since the site covers kindergarten through 12th grade.
Watch the email address you give, because the team reaches out to arrange the match.
For college help, pick a specific area from the list, such as AP courses, SAT or ACT, or financial aid.
Ask about session length and cost before you commit, since the pages do not state them.

records.notes: Tier 1 recorded a 2026-08 blog date that this visit could not confirm. The newest blog post with a year written next to its date is dated Dec 11, 2025, so that is recorded. Newer posts show dates with no year, and one title reads Summer Reading Programs 2026, but neither is used because no year is written next to a date. The footer copyright reads 2022 and is not evidence. The contact page gives only Philadelphia, PA 19107, with no street address. No price, session length or schedule is published, so no cost or schedule is recorded.

notes: Seven groups, all verdict publish. Fetches used: 28 (Liberty 4, Youth Action 5, Cheer Elite 4, Girls Baseball 3, Rebel Ventures 4, Restore 4, RISE 4). No pages were blocked and no rate limiting was seen. One WebSearch used of the 1 allowed, for Philadelphia Youth Action's 2026 application status; it found no 2026 to 2027 application notice, and the program pages still name 2024 to 2025. Main tier 1 corrections: Liberty drill fee and New Jersey venue added; Philly Cheer Elite fee wording fixed; Restore's Circle of Care page is a donation form, not a request form; RISE last sign of life moved to 2025-12 because the 2026-08 date could not be seen on the blog. The Liberty event page's body text conflicts with its header and was handled as noted in that record.
